text: The book drop was a milk crate by the back door. Every Thursday, around two o'clock, Imre would find something that wasn't milk. First week, A Field Guide to Mushrooms of the Northeast, Carver Street Library stamp on the flyleaf, due date long past. Second week, same book. Third week, same. He'd stopped reshelving it in his head. It lived on the flour bench now, between the scale and the rye starter, cover gone soft with thumbprints. Tonight he slid the crate out with his hip, oven mitts on. The book was there again, heavier than usual. A yellow square of paper stuck out around page 112. He peeled off the mitts. The note was in pencil, small, slanted hard to the right. "Your door smells better than the library. I keep meaning to bring it to the right place. Is the morel on this page the one you use? -T." Imre looked at the page. The morel sat there, wrinkled and brown. He pulled the pencil from behind his ear, flipped the note over, and wrote "No. Never used one." Then, after a moment, he added "Come at five, there's bread." He pressed it back into the book.
